Since the case submodules area used in various case record like complaint case, inspection, further investigation, field surveillance, overall scanning, individual scanning, there is a need of centralized module to handle and manage all common case submodules. Objectives

Objectives Folders This sub-module allows users to upload labelled documents to different Folders (using a table column/drop-down list) and track them all in a listing page for documentation purpose.This sub-module will have the following folders: a.AA – Inspectorʼs Report/Summary of Case/Statement of Facts b.A – Feedback/Complaint Form (Only 1 document can be uploaded to Folder A.This will not be populated from the Feedback or Complaint.) c.A – Statements of Complainants and Witnesses d.B – Statements of Person(s) of Interest e.C – Investigation Diary f.D – Documents g.
E – Other Enclosures (Including Update of Case Outcome to Complainant/Letters Issued to POI) By default, the folders table listing will be sorted by Folder in alphabetical order, then Created Date and time in chronological order. default, the listing page will show 100 items.Each time a document is uploaded, the user can also manually input the type of document, which will be captured in the listing page.The type of document will determine the additional information needed when uploading the document (e.g.Name of POI/EOI when selecting NFA document type).Only the uploaders themselves can delete a document.This will be tracked in the activity log.When a document record is created, the User can upload multiple attachments.From the listing page, if the attachments are clicked, all the attachments will be downloaded.Users can select the documents they wish to download with the checkboxes and click on the “Download Selected” button to immediately begin the download.

Here, he is choosing the template that will be created by selecting one of the 2 radio buttons: “Summary of Facts” or “Inspector Report”.After which, he will be brought to the page where he can edit the template, enter his content and save the report.For any value that has no value when pulled for pre-population, the tokens should be replaced with a blank.All 4 case report tabs will have the same behavior with regards to creation and editing of reports unless otherwise stated.Once the documents are saved as final, its contents cannot be changed.The system will provide a function to review the documents.The “Edit” button will duplicate the documentʼs content and will allow the user to edit the content as a new document.The system will support versioning fo

When the user chooses to save as final, the system will record the date and time, and mark the document as version n, where n is a running number. Every time the user edits a final document or creates a new document, and then saves as final, n will be increased by 1.E.g.DDI clicks on “Edit” on Inspector Report v1, and after amending, clicks on “Save as final”, it will be saved as Inspector Report v2.Final versions can have a letter template generated from the completed document.Clicking on the “Print” button will open a new window to display the file preview containing the content within the RTE and format based on CEA letter format.The format for Recommendations is as seen in the Template field, and will have pagination.There will be an RTE for the user to write all case report documents.The user will navigate to the appropriate tab before creating the corresponding documen

fence/Breach>” header onwards should be included to be printed.Reply to POI/EOI and Reply to Complainant is provided for the user to prepare a letter or an email to the POI/EOI/Complainant about the case outcome.

The pre-populated list of values for the offences and breaches will be the long values based on mapping to the selected short values from the case. The mapping and long valuesʼ content will be configurable from the Code Maintenance module.All communications and reply to or from the complainant/feedback provider will be logged in the Correspondences tab in the form of listing.Please refer to ACEAS Requirement Specifications – Feedback and Complaint Management for more information.Persons This sub-module allows users to add or remove Persons in a case.Each case can have a maximum of 30 Persons.This was previously discussed and agreed within CEA.The Person can be a salesperson or non-salesperson, and witness or POI.By default, the Persons ta

EA.The Person can be a salesperson or non-salesperson, and witness or POI.By default, the Persons table listing will be sorted by Personʼs Name in chronological order of creation.Users must first search for a personʼs profile and retrieve it before he can add it to the case.
Clicking on the “Search” button after user has entered the name of the Person (based on the NRIC) he wishes to search and retrieve will show a pop-up modal, with the results of the search in the form of a table. The table will include some information (e.g.Name of Individual, NRIC, Registration Number (if any), Name of Current EA (if any), etc.(Please refer to ACEAS Requirement Specifications – Common UI section 3.9 (Search and Retrieve)) and an action button.A note will sit in the modal to guide users to retrieve a profile and allow users to create a profile from Profile Management if a Person does not currently have one in ACEAS.On this page, users can click on the name of the individual or name of current EA, wh

e one in ACEAS.On this page, users can click on the name of the individual or name of current EA, which will open a new window to the Personʼs profile inside the profile management module to verify this is the right person, if more information is required.The Action column allows users to add the selected person to the case.
Users can then click on “+” icon to retrieve who they wish to add as a person to this case. After retrieval, the Name field will be disabled.The user will see the following detailed information: a.Type of Person (POI or Witness) b.Personʼs Name c.Personʼs NRIC d.Personʼs Registration Number (if any) e.Personʼs EA Employment Information (if applicable) The persons form will have a “clear” function to be used if the wrong personʼs details are retrieved.After successfully adding a person to the case, the user will be brought to a view page with the following information: a.Type of Person b.Personʼs Role c.Case Status d.Personʼs Name e.Personʼs NRIC f.Personʼs RES Regi

: a.Type of Person b.Personʼs Role c.Case Status d.Personʼs Name e.Personʼs NRIC f.Personʼs RES Registration No.(if applicable) g.Personʼs Licence Expiry Date (if applicable) h.Personʼs Contact Information i.Personʼs EA Employment Information (if applicable) j.CEA Watch List Status k.Current/Past Compliant/Complaint Records including Last Action Taken Date for the past 2 years.

NFA/LOR/LOA/LOW – Date Issued b.Composition of Offence – Payment Date c.LOC/FP – Notice of Decision d.Disciplinary Committee – Conviction Date e.Court Prosecution – Conviction Date l.Investigation Outcome POI will have “save” function to update editable fields.Persons will have “delete” function to remove them as a POI or Witness.For Witnesses, there will be a “Convert to POI” button which when clicked, will change the Witnessʼ “Type of Person” to POI.All the Statements in the Folders sub-module with the Witnessʼ name in the “Name of POI/Witness” column which w

tements in the Folders sub-module with the Witnessʼ name in the “Name of POI/Witness” column which were in Folder A will be changed to Folder B.Entities This sub-module allows users to add or remove Entities in a case and is similar to the Persons module.The difference between Entities and Persons are as follows.The Entities added to the case may or may not have relation with the persons added in Persons.
Similar with Persons sub-module, when adding an Entity to the case, users will first have to search for an Entity, and then retrieve it. The Entity Search table will include some information (e.g.Name of Entity, UEN, Name of KEO, etc.(Please refer to ACEAS Requirement Specifications – Common UI section 3.9 (Search and Retrieve)) and an action button to retrieve the desired Entityʼs profile to be added to the case.The system will also provide a redirection to the profile management module to facilitate the user to create a new profile for an Entity that does not currently exist in ACEA

Statements This sub-module allows users to create a statement and a further statement for each Person.For each Person, there can be only one 1st statement created.However, there can be multiple further statements created.The creation of further statements will only happen when a Person already has a 1st statement recorded.a.Statement (Witness) b.Statement (POI) c.Further Statement The statement gen

1st statement recorded.a.Statement (Witness) b.Statement (POI) c.Further Statement The statement generated will depend on whether the Person is a witness or POI.For further statements, there is only one letter template.By default, the statements table listing will be sorted by Name of POI/Witness, followed by Created Date and Time in chronological order.The table will thus group all statements from one POI or Witness (depending on the tab which the user is at) together, and then arrange them by “Created Date and Time” in chronological order.
Users must click “Create” from the Statements – POI or Witnesses tab and choose a POI/Witness based on the Persons and Directors/Shareholders of the Entities added to the Complaint Case. The system will check whether a 1st statement exists for the specific Person.If no statement exists, the system will generate the letter template for the 1st statement.If a statement already exists, the system will generate the letter template for a further stateme

nt.If a statement already exists, the system will generate the letter template for a further statement.The documents will have “save as draft” and “end the statement” function.The draft will only exist in the system for 30 days from the date it was created, date it was last auto-saved, or date “save as draft” was clicked.After that, the draft will be removed.The statements will have “delete” function if its status is “draft”.There will be tokens provided in the declaration section of the statement, that auto populates the No.of pages, and the statement signed date and time.
While the statement is in the draft status, this content is still editable. dDateandTime% This pulls the date and time of when “Submit” is clicked when the statement is in “Ended” state When the user chooses to end the statement, the system will record the date and time, and the statement will not be editable.The statement will support electronic signing function on a tablet and generation to PDF (by clicking “generate”) to obtain a physical signature after selecting “end the statement”.If electronic signature is selected, the witness will sign directly on the statement using a stylus (for example).An indicator will be provided when the statement is signed and selecting “Sign”.
Once completed, the statement will be digitally signed using CEAʼs SSL certificate to ensure integrity of the document and the user can upload/save the digitally signed document in the system. If the statement is generated as PDF, printed, then signed physically, the user must check that the statement was signed physically, indicate the signed date and time and upload the necessary docu

the statement was signed physically, indicate the signed date and time and upload the necessary document(s).“Submit” will then be selected to indicate that the statement was signed.Ended and Signed statements can be generated into PDF documents.Clicking on the “Print” button will open a new window to display the file preview containing the formatted statements page.The Statements/Further Statements includes the RTE and digital signing fields, and will have pagination.Case Exhibits This sub-module allows users to create forms that track the deposit/withdrawal of case exhibits in a listing.
It also allows users to track individual case exhibits that have been deposited in the store, and their current whereabouts/status. There will be the following two tabs: a.List of Exhibits b.Case Exhibit Movement Upon seizing a case exhibit, the OIC will fill out the Acknowledgement Slip offline, with the person whom he is seizing the case exhibit from.Then he will create an Exhibit Form on ACEAS, sel

he person whom he is seizing the case exhibit from.Then he will create an Exhibit Form on ACEAS, select the type of form, the type of deposit/withdrawal, fill in details of the items seized, and upload his Acknowledgement Slip and forward the case exhibit deposit request to the Store Manager in system.The form will have “save as draft” function.The draft will only exist in the system for 30 days from the date it was created, date it was last auto-saved, or date “save as draft” was clicked.After that, the draft will be removed.The form will allow for users to enter item description, value and how disposed of fields.Users can add more items up to 50.
This duplicates the 5 fields each time. By default, the case exhibits forms table listing will be sorted by descending “Created Date and Time”.The Case Exhibit Forms will have “delete” function if its status is “draft”.OIC will then submit this form to the SM to respond on a centralized Store Management Module.The SM can choose the following

s form to the SM to respond on a centralized Store Management Module.The SM can choose the following actions: a.Acknowledge b.Reject c.Rework If the SM acknowledges the OICʼs Case Exhibit Form deposit request, they must sign digitally.After acknowledgement, the System will record the information about the decision made: a.Case Exhibit number (system generated) b.Taking Over Date and Time c.Store Managerʼs Name d.Status e.Remarks (if any) If the SM chooses to rework, the form will be sent back to the OIC to make amends on the original form.If the SM chooses to reject, the form will be sent back to the OIC with the rejection details.
After completing the Deposit process, the items from the Case Exhibit Form will be listed in the Case Exhibit Items tab. The List of Exhibits will be sorted by Date and Time of First Deposit in chronological order.This value is captured when the Store Manager first acknowledges the Case Exhibit Items deposit form.This date and time value will not change even

first acknowledges the Case Exhibit Items deposit form.This date and time value will not change even as the exhibit is withdrawn and redeposited.The movement of the item is tracked in the Exhibit Status column.The process to return the Case Exhibit Item(s) are similar to depositing the items, with the following differences.The OIC will create an Exhibit Form on ACEAS, select the type of form, the type of deposit/withdrawal, and select the items to be returned.The OIC will then submit this form to the SM to respond on a centralized Store Management Module.After the SM/OIC receives the exhibits from the OIC/SM in person, he/she will tally with the items listed in the request form and acknowledge in system.

cess will be complete.File Movement This sub-module tracks the physical movement of the physical folder of documents related to this case on a list.The information populating this list is pulled from the centralised File Movement Module.Clicking on the view button on the listing will direct users to the detailed page of the file movement record in the File Movement List module.If a user wishes to create a new File Movement entry, he has to do it on the File Movement List module detailed in section File Movement List.Only authorised users can create and edit File Movement entries.Case Exhibit List There are two sub-modules under the Case Exhibits List module: Case Exhibit Forms, and Case Exhibit Items.The Case Exhibit Forms list collates all the Case Exhibit Forms from all the various cases in ACEAS.
The Case Exhibit Items list collates all the Case Exhibit Items from all the various cases in ACEAS. File Movement List This module allows users to create and track File Movements.These fil

s in ACEAS.
